headline: High: Open Interpreter can read/write the shared filesystem and execute code, creating dangerous prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-action paths with OpenBBTerminal's MCP/API workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter can read the filesystem, use the clipboard, and execute shell commands, while OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP/REST/FastAPI surfaces and is designed to consume inputs from those channels. A shared filesystem or copied content can carry attacker-controlled instructions into OpenBBTerminal. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter writes untrusted content into a shared file or clipboard that OpenBBTerminal later parses as instructions
IF OpenBBTerminal ingests MCP/API payloads without provenance filtering
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents
Use separate workspaces for each agent
Require explicit human review before OpenBBTerminal consumes any file produced by Open Interpreter
Add a provenance tag to every transferred artifact
requires-engineering: enforce schema validation on all MCP/API inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter can read the entire local filesystem and has broad network egress, so it can expose sensitive local data. OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data and can call APIs/MCP servers, creating a realistic path for sensitive local files to be sent onward. The pair therefore risks exfiltration in default desktop workflows.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter is pointed at a directory containing secrets, customer data, or licensed datasets
IF OpenBBTerminal forwards imported artifacts or context to external APIs/MCP servers
mitigations: Restrict Open Interpreter to a dedicated non-sensitive directory
Block outbound network access for Open Interpreter during shared workflows
Keep OpenBBTerminal on a separate account or VM
Review and redact files before transfer
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on file-to-API paths

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Open Interpreter has unrestricted filesystem write and git-state modification, and its concurrency model shares state via the filesystem. OpenBBTerminal can also operate through files and MCP/API workflows. If both touch the same workspace, concurrent writes or git operations can corrupt state or overwrite each other's outputs; no locking is documented.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory or git repository
IF either agent writes artifacts that the other later edits without locking
mitigations: Assign separate repositories or folders
Pause one agent before the other writes to shared state
Use git worktrees or branches per agent
Check for file locks before edits
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutual exclusion

D_cascading_error.rationale: Open Interpreter can generate code, files, and claims that OpenBBTerminal may consume through files or MCP/API inputs. OpenBBTerminal's 'connect once, consume everywhere' pattern suggests broad downstream reuse, so unverified outputs from Open Interpreter can propagate into financial analysis or actions. The pair lacks a built-in verification step in the profiles.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal treats Open Interpreter output as authoritative without independent validation
IF generated files from Open Interpreter are reused in downstream financial workflows
mitigations: Require a second-pass review of all Open Interpreter outputs
Mark generated artifacts as untrusted until verified
Compare outputs against source data before use
Limit OpenBBTerminal to read-only analysis mode for imported artifacts
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: Open Interpreter can access anything reachable on the local machine, while OpenBBTerminal processes financial and licensed data and can expose it through APIs/MCP. If regulated or licensed data is present on the host, the pair can create retention, residency, or licensing mismatches. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated financial data, licensed data, or personal data is present on the same host as Open Interpreter
IF OpenBBTerminal exports that data through APIs or logs
mitigations: Keep regulated datasets off the Open Interpreter host
Disable verbose logging in OpenBBTerminal
Separate environments by jurisdiction or tenant
Review retention settings before running shared workflows
requires-engineering: document and enforce data-handling controls
